newsitem.title: INDIA: India says petroleum sector needs huge investments.
newsitem.headline: India says petroleum sector needs huge investments.

text.p: The harnessing of India's petroleum resources calls for huge investments, sophisticated technology and sustained industrial growth, junior Petroleum Minister T.R. Balu said on Thursday.

"Increasing demand of petroleum products (is) forcing the national oil companies to look beyond...both within their territories and outside," Balu told an international petroleum technology conference in the Indian capital.
Balu said in written remarks prepared for delivery at the conference that India's demand for petroleum products was rising at a substantial rate of 6 to 7 percent annually.

Industry Minister Murasoli Maran said the government, recognising the urgent need to expand exploration activities, had invited private firms, both domestic and international, to supplement the efforts of national oil companies.

"Oil and gas field services and services incidental to mining such as drilling, shafting, reclamation, surveys and mapping have been included in the expanded list of automatic foreign equity participation up to 74 percent," Maran said in a statement.
"These initiatives, we think, will narrow down the gap between the demand and domestic availability," Maran said.
Maran pointed out the index of industrial production for crude petroleum and refinery products accounted for nearly four percent of overall industrial growth.
"This is an indication of how critically shortages in this sector affect overall production," he said.
